messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Your heart rate should be monitored.
Diabetes or long gaps without food.
Metoprolol can hide the early warning signs of low blood sugar, such as a fast heartbeat.
Metoprolol can make low blood sugar more severe or last longer.
The risk is higher if you are fasting, not eating regularly, or vomiting.
An overactive thyroid.
Metoprolol can mask signs of an overactive thyroid.
Stopping it suddenly can trigger a thyroid crisis.
Circulation problems in your arms or legs.
Beta blockers can make symptoms of poor circulation worse.
A history of severe allergic reactions.
If you have anaphylaxis while taking a beta blocker.
The usual dose of injectable epinephrine may not work as well.
Pheochromocytoma (a tumor of the adrenal gland).
Metoprolol must only be started after an alpha blocker has been started.
Otherwise, blood pressure can rise sharply.
Liver disease.
Metoprolol is broken down by the liver, so levels can build up.
Treatment is usually started at a lower dose.
Surgery.
Tell your surgeon and dentist that you take metoprolol.
Triples: [["Metoprolol", "has administration instruction", "monitor heart rate"], ["Metoprolol", "has warning", "diabetes or long gaps without food"], ["Metoprolol", "can mask", "early warning signs of low blood sugar"], ["Metoprolol", "can worsen", "low blood sugar severity or duration"], ["Metoprolol", "increased risk in", "fasting, not eating regularly, or vomiting"], ["Metoprolol", "can mask", "signs of overactive thyroid"], ["Metoprolol", "has warning", "stopping suddenly can trigger thyroid crisis"], ["Metoprolol", "can worsen", "circulation problems in arms or legs"], ["Metoprolol", "has warning", "history of severe allergic reactions"], ["Metoprolol", "interacts with", "anaphylaxis"], ["Metoprolol", "reduces effectiveness of", "injectable epinephrine"], ["Metoprolol", "has contraindication", "pheochromocytoma"], ["Metoprolol", "requires prior use of", "alpha blocker"], ["Metoprolol", "has warning", "blood pressure can rise sharply if not started with alpha blocker"], ["Metoprolol", "has contraindication", "liver disease"], ["Metoprolol", "metabolized by", "liver"], ["Metoprolol", "has administration instruction", "treatment usually started at lower dose"], ["Metoprolol", "has administration instruction", "tell surgeon and dentist about use"]]
Relations: ["can mask", "can worsen", "has administration instruction", "has contraindication", "has warning", "increased risk in", "interacts with", "metabolized by", "reduces effectiveness of", "requires prior use of"]
Answer:

completion:
can mask: The subject drug may conceal or hide the symptoms or signs specified by the object entity.  
can worsen: The subject drug may increase the severity or negative impact of the condition or symptom specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the specific action or instruction specified by the object entity to be followed during its use.  
has contraindication: The subject drug should not be used in patients with the condition or situation specified by the object entity.  
has warning: The subject drug is associated with a specific caution or risk that patients should be aware of, as specified by the object entity.  
increased risk in: The subject drug may pose a greater risk or have more severe effects in patients with the condition or situation specified by the object entity.  
interacts with: The subject drug may have a pharmacological interaction with the condition or substance specified by the object entity, potentially altering its effects.  
metabolized by: The subject drug is processed or broken down by the organ or system specified by the object entity.  
reduces effectiveness of: The subject drug may decrease the efficacy or potency of the substance or treatment specified by the object entity.  
requires prior use of: The subject drug must be initiated only after the substance or treatment specified by the object entity has been used.
